title: Neighborhood preference; childhood chores and family roles
description: The interviewee explains why she prefers her current home to Potlatch, emphasizing space, privacy, and freedom to keep animals. She then recalls family life while growing up, especially the uneven division of chores among siblings and the heavy responsibilities of her sister Janice.

title: Changing family life; Potlatch social order and school years
description: She says families have changed, with better material conditions but less parental discipline. The conversation moves to the scale and social divisions of Potlatch, then to her school years and the fact that she grew up around her future husband without really knowing him at the time.

title: Courtship; marriage; housing and town upkeep
description: The interviewee describes an on-and-off courtship before marriage and the simple expectations she had for married life. The interviewer also asks about Potlatch as a company town and the condition of houses and buildings there.

title: Starting a family; doctors and hospital care
description: She talks about getting married and having children without detailed planning. The discussion then turns to medical services, including traveling to Moscow for hospital care and memories of birth practices before her own children were born.

title: Having twins; later childbirth experiences
description: The interviewee recounts learning she was having twins, feeling frightened, and suffering complications after their birth. She compares that difficult delivery to easier births of her later children and discusses their low birth weights.

title: Janitor work; leisure and movies
description: She describes her job cleaning a school and some of the practical differences between buildings she has worked in. The conversation then shifts to limited free time, family outings, and inexpensive recreation such as movies.

title: Close family; expectations for children; gardening
description: The interviewee says her family is close and that she and her children help each other. She discusses her mother, the lack of pressure when she quit school, her own relationship with her mother, and plans for a large garden.

title: Water and sewer improvements; religion; city versus small town
description: She explains that her area recently gained water and sewer service after earlier reliance on wells and septic tanks. She then says she does not attend church and argues that small towns are safer, friendlier, and more community-minded than cities.

title: Oregon move; husband's military service; raising children through change
description: The interviewee recalls a brief stay in Oregon for her husband's work and her preference for returning home. She talks about managing while he was overseas in the service, raising her children with help from family, and reflects on how earlier hardships shaped different generations.
